summary: Intermittent 429 bursts for multiplexed websocket chat causing degraded UX
description: Issue summary: NimbusHealth is seeing intermittent bursts of HTTP 429 responses returned to multiplexed websocket clients on the hosted API during peak business hours. Impact: Users in their clinical triage chat are experiencing message failures and UI retries, increasing perceived latency and leading to dropped conversations. Scope: Affects ~10 client connection pools from NimbusHealth (enterprise account) in us-east region; seen across redwood-chat-small and medium models. Expected: Multiplexed websocket connections should see smoothing by token-level and connection-level rate limits with transparent backpressure, not sudden 429 bursts. Observed: Spikes of 429s lasting 20-40s every ~15 minutes, correlating with bursty fan-out from a single internal service. Steps to reproduce: 1) Establish multiplexed websocket session using shared API key for multiple browser clients (as customer implemented). 2) Simulate parallel message bursts (20 simultaneous requests over the same websocket multiplex) with messages that produce ~80-200 tokens. 3) Observe intermittent 429 responses returned with X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 and Retry-After headers. Logs: Attached sample gateway headers and rate-limiter trace (see comment #2). Customer note: This started after migration to a client-side multiplexer used to reduce websocket count. Customer requests guidance on configuration to avoid disruption without dramatically lowering throughput.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: shared API key + multiplexing causes client-level bucket exhaustion because token and concurrency limits are aggregated per-API key in current rate-limiter config. Evidence: Rate-limiter traces show single token bucket hit (bucket_id=acct-nimbushealth) with short refill cycles; connection-level counters spike to 100+ concurrent inflight requests. API gateway metrics indicate per-key bursts coincide with 429 timestamps. Alternate hypothesis: upstream quota-service mis-evaluating multiplexed connection headers; less likely given consistent bucket_id. Mitigation applied: temporarily increased per-key burst window for NimbusHealth from 200 to 500 tokens for 2 hours via emergency override (PR referenced). Next steps: implement per-connection bucketing (split by websocket connection-id) as a more robust fix and add an opt-in config for enterprises using multiplexers. Engineering owner: Liam O'Connor (rate-limiter). Related work: design doc draft in linked Confluence page.

resolution_notes: Short-term: emergency per-key burst uplift applied for NimbusHealth while engineering builds a connection-scoped bucket model. Medium-term: roadmap item to support optional per-connection and per-subscription rate-limiter keys for enterprise customers using multiplexers. Action items: 1) Engineering to ship connection-bucketing change and add integration tests (owner: Liam O'Connor). 2) Support to publish best-practice note: avoid sharing API key across high-fanout multiplex clients; prefer per-client subkeys or per-connection tokens. 3) Postmortem/learnings to Confluence and notify account team before uplift revert.
